Compact dual tails then give uniform H_U→fvee and L1 f*q_U→f; countably choosing pairs meeting both numerical error bounds and applying Riesz–Fischer proves global a.e. equality without a countable neighborhood base. Haar positivity proves unique continuous representative and equality at each continuity point. Zero f and discrete/trivial groups check. The observed draft B-page asserts that point changes always preserve the L1 class and that inversion cannot ever recover arbitrary representatives everywhere. On a finite discrete group every singleton has mass 1/N, so point changes alter the class and finite inversion holds everywhere. On nondiscrete G the reviewed counterexample proves singleton Haar-nullity, making such changes valid. Corrected page prose states nondiscreteness and the actual failure to recover every representative.
